== Biography ==
== Research Notes ==
=== Peoria family evidence, 23 October 2026 ===

The published obituary transcription identifies Samuel Steel Glasgow, then in his ninetieth year, as the surviving brother of [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Glasgow]] of Hanna City. The distinctive name and age fit [[Glasgow-9|Samuel Steele Glasgow]], born in September 1814. Stewart’s established Peoria family and independently reviewed 94% paternal identification with [[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] support extending the same father to this documented brother. This is a confident combined paternal inference, not a literal statement naming Samuel’s father in the obituary. 92% is a subjective assessment of the complete Samuel-9 to Robert-8 father identification. The obituary supplies the sibling relationship; the 1880 county sketch and 1925 family interview comparisons identify Stewart and support his father. The Peoria Star abstract and Monmouth Review account quoting the Peoria Herald Transcript may derive from one obituary and are not counted as independent parentage witnesses. Published transcription inspected; original newspaper image uninspected. Mother and all vital fields remain separately assessed.

The documented brother is [[Glasgow-9|Samuel Steele Glasgow]], whose father placement under [[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] is reassessed 92%. Stewart’s existing 94% assessment is unchanged.

<ref>WeRelate, Stewart Glasgow biography: Peoria Star, 24 August 1904, abridged by a genealogy society; and Monmouth Review, 24 August 1904, quoting the Peoria Herald Transcript, surviving brother Samuel Steel Glasgow passage. [https://www.werelate.org/wiki/Person:Stewart_Glasgow_(1) Published transcription], inspected 23 October 2026; original uninspected.</ref>

=== Peoria family and parentage ===

The separately assessed mother [[Finley-134]] is confidently assessed at 94%: 90% → 94%; named maternity with the newly strengthened [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]] adult identity. The parent ratings share their identity evidence.


The previously inspected 1925 recollection names [[Glasgow-8|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Finley-134|Rosanna Finley]] as parents of [[Glasgow-16|Finley]] and [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]]. Newly inspected vol. 15 pp. 98–99 identifies that [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]] as [[Glasgow-16|Finley]]’s brother in Peoria with first wife Elizabeth Askain [transcriber’s best guess]; p. 120 adds his son [[Glasgow-1923|Huston]]. The original 1880 Peoria sketch independently names Stewart, born in Adams County in 1823, first wife [[Askren-120|Elizabeth Askren]] and son [[Glasgow-1923|Huston]], followed by [[Wiley-3632|Hadessah Wyley]] and the matching later children. These specific relatives bridge the previously qualified [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]]-to-Stewart adult identity. The county sketch does not itself name Stewart’s parents.<ref>The History of Peoria County, Illinois (Chicago: Johnson & Company, 1880), pp. 791–792, Stewart Glasgow sketch. [https://archive.org/details/historyofpeoriac00john/page/791/mode/1up Read source]. Original printed county-history pages, Internet Archive leaves 853–854; visually inspected. A contemporary biographical account, not a birth register; informant not identified.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, pp. 98–99; Martha Melvina Glasgow household interview, 24 October 1925; library transcription, PDF p. 658. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=658 Read source]. Modern library transcription of a dated interview, visually inspected; not a manuscript facsimile. Retrospective recollection contains a wrong recent-death estimate and an incomplete later-wife account.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, p. 120; Stuart Glasgow family recollection, 25 October 1925; library transcription, PDF p. 668. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=668 Read source]. Modern library transcription of a dated interview, visually inspected; not a manuscript facsimile. Names Stuart’s son Huston and uncle Finley, but his reported age 26 conflicts with the county sketch and held dates.</ref>

The existing father is confidently assessed at 94%. 94% is a subjective assessment of the complete existing father/profile pair, combining named retrospective parentage with a contemporary adult-family identity comparison. The interviews can share family tradition. The 1880 sketch prints Stewart’s birth as 23 April 1823, versus the retained 13 April field. It says Huston died aged 24; the 1925 recollection says 26, while the retained 23 August 1848–15 October 1871 dates imply 23. The 1925 account’s death “2 or 3 years ago” also conflicts with Stewart’s retained 1904 death, and its “second wife” Edith omits Hadassah. The matching Peoria residence, first wife and son identify the family despite these specific errors; none supplies authority to overwrite the dates. Inspect Faris p. 63 and original death/marriage records to resolve them.


=== Earlier parent review — superseded below ===

Rosanna [[Finley-134|Finley]] is separately assessed as his mother at 90%, because the 1925 account explicitly calls her mother of Finley and Stuart. That identification shares the stated child-identity limits; the two parent percentages are not independent probabilities.

The 24 October 1925 household interview records [[Finley-134|Rosanna Finley]], wife of Robert Glasgow, as mother of Finley and Stuart Glasgow. Finley is independently anchored to the Campbell-wife/Weldon family by the 1925 Ora and 1926 Samuel interviews. [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Steele Glasgow]] is the existing 1823 Adams County to Peoria account with exactly this named couple and brother; no checked alternative Stuart has that family. This explicit combined family statement strengthens the inherited placement beyond its previous name-and-generation fit.<ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, p. 101; Robert Arthur Glasgow household interview, 24 October 1925; library transcription, PDF p. 659. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=659 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 18, pp. 259–260; Samuel Steele Glasgow interview, 1 October 1926; library transcription, PDF pp. 1619–1620. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=1619 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, pp. 310–313; Idelma Ora Glasgow interview, 3 November 1925; library transcription, PDF pp. 759–761. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=760 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref>

The existing father is confidently assessed at 90%. 90% is a subjective confident assessment for the complete Stewart-profile/father pair. Stuart is the literal source form. The recollection supplies neither his age nor wife; identification with the later Stewart remains inferred and is less fully anchored than Finley’s. The informant reports her mother’s recollection. Thompson’s ensuing inferred upper pedigree, including a Robert said to die about 1806, is not adopted. No other alleged sibling or older ancestor gains confidence from this review.


=== Earlier father review, 22 October 2026 — superseded below ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-8]] is assessed at 79% (probable). Stewart Steele’s 13 April 1823 birth and distinctive middle name fit Robert Barclay Glasgow and Rosanna Finley’s Adams County family account, including the earlier William and Martha entries.

Probable specific family placement; a transcribed contemporary parent record is not held in this capture.

Next useful test: Find Stewart in Robert’s family register or probate child list.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-17 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-17]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
